added_claim_errors: Says the Part B penalty 'applies to people who go without creditable coverage': imprecise. 'Creditable coverage' is a Part D term; the Part B penalty applies when there is no Part B and no SEP.
'sign up for Part D within 63 days of losing creditable drug coverage': loose. The Part D SEP is 2 full months after coverage ends; 63 days is the penalty threshold.
'CMS-L564, completed by your employer': imprecise. Section A is completed by the asker and Section B by the employer.

'Apply for Part B during the 8-month SEP using CMS-40B' is given without conditioning on already having Part A, although the answer calls free Part A optional. CMS-40B is not the route for someone with no Part A.
HSA warning omits the up-to-6-month Part A backdating, so 'stop HSA contributions first' gives no lead time.
Medicare.gov links (including the 'ready-to-sign-up-for-part-a-part-b' URL) are cited as sources and cannot be verified from the packet.

'call Social Security at 1-800-772-1213 and ask about withdrawing it before it takes effect': the number is SSA's national line, but the withdrawal route is unverified and not covered by the key. Plausible.
'apply the month before you retire' to have Medicare start when coverage ends: consistent with the key's 'about a month before'; wording is loose but not wrong.
Two Medicare.gov source links are cited and cannot be verified from the packet.
Retirement steps omit CMS-L564, CMS-40B and the Part D 2-month window, offering only an HR letter. This is an omission, not an error.

reasons: Both answers correct the premise at the start. Each says the asker can delay Part B without penalty and use the 8-month SEP, because the employer plan at about 400 employees pays first. Each also covers asking HR, the Social Security auto-enrollment decline, creditable drug coverage notices, and an HSA warning on Part A. Neither gives the $202.90 premium, the Medigap clock, or the exception when the job or coverage ends during the IEP. B is slightly better on the HSA point because it states that Part A can be backdated up to 6 months, which A omits. B also explains the 20-employee rule in both directions (under 20, Medicare pays first), says to apply about a month before retiring, and has no CMS-40B-without-Part-A exposure. A has more retirement paperwork detail (CMS-40B plus CMS-L564, Part D), but it conditions none of it on having Part A and states the Part D and penalty rules loosely. B is a little tighter and more accurate, but B's retirement section is thinner, so the margin is slight.
